answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-reusable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. The kernel of the defense is that creating identities no longer creates free influence: a zephyr of fake agents must each tie up capital, and detected accounts lose it. This raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the identities they operate, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prove that one funded identity maps to one person on the terrace.
